Activity.description: What a lane is doing now, literally.

oneOf.description: The command's first line, `cd x &&` stripped.
Repo-relative.
A file read, or a search when `pattern` is set.
Any other tool. For an MCP server's tool, `server` names the server and `name` its tool.
A web fetch (`detail` the host) or search (`detail` the query).
Updating its own todo list.
Assistant text streamed in the last 3 s.
A run is active with nothing open and no text for 3 s: waiting on the model.

fix.description: The command a person runs to fix it, when there is one.

message.description: Plain words: what is installed, or what is wrong.

AndroidState.description: Where a node's android sessions stand, for the doctor.

oneOf.description: Installed, with KVM usable: sessions start.
Not installed yet; the first android `session_start` installs it.
Can't run here until a person fixes something (no KVM, or the install failed).

AppError.description: A `call` failed, or (without `id`) the session did.

oneOf.description: Sent once the key is accepted.

features.description: The newer client messages it reads ([`APP_FEATURES`]). Absent from older hubs: send them none.

version.description: The hub's fleetd version, as hub_info reports it. Absent from older hubs.

oneOf.description: Answer to `snapshot`: the fleetd_status data.
A `call` succeeded; `output` is the tool's output.
On the live subscription only. Ephemeral: a slow link drops intermediate frames.
On the chat subscription only: the lead's reply as it streams. Ephemeral and never replayed.
On the browser watch only: the watched session's newest screen. Ephemeral: a slow link drops frames.

Attention.description:
Whether an event needs the human now, set by the hub when it emits the event. "loud": notify, but hold it through
quiet hours; "urgent": notify even during quiet hours (money and irreversible). Absent: the inbox and the digest
are enough.

BrowserControl.description:
Who drives a live session's browser. A person takes it over (human) and hands it back (handing_back, until the
agent's next tool call sees the page as the person left it, then agent). While it isn't the agent's, the agent's
browser tools answer that a person has control.

BrowserFrame.description:
One screencast frame of a live session, for the person watching. Ephemeral: the hub keeps only the newest per
session, and a slow link skips frames rather than queueing them.

seq.description: 1, 2, ... per watch; a frame older than one already shown is dropped.

url.description: The page the frame shows, when the node knows it.

width.description: The image's size in pixels: `browser_input` coordinates are in it.

ChatDelta.description:
Streamed text of the subscribed chat's lead message `messageId`. `offset` is the message's text length before
`append`, in UTF-16 units: append when it equals the length the app holds, skip the frame when
`offset + append.length` is within it (already applied, e.g. after a `chat_history` read), and read the message
again otherwise (a gap). The `chat.message` event with `state: final` carries the full text.

ChatOpenItem.description: An inline item that waits on the human: which message, and what it asks for.

ChatOpenNudge.description: A nudge still waiting, in a chat state: its message, and what to look at.

DesktopBackend.description:
Where a desktop session's apps run: in a fresh container of the node's pinned image (docker or podman), or as the
node's user on an Xvfb display of their own with a fresh home directory.

backend.description: What sessions run in: a container where the node has docker or podman, else Xvfb.

fix.description: The command a person runs to fix it, when there is one.

message.description: Plain words: what sessions use, or what is missing.

DesktopState.description: Where a node's Linux desktop sessions stand, for the doctor.

oneOf.description: The container runtime is building the pinned image.
Neither a container runtime nor an Xvfb, or the image failed to build.

attention.description: Latest failed, waiting and usage-limited events, and PRs the merge train sent back to their authors.

chats.description: Each project's chat: whether its lead waits on you, whether it works. Absent from hubs without chat.

notify.description: When to notify the human; absent from older hubs.

slots.description: Absent until the hub runs the slot board (M5).

HostCheck.description:
Whether a machine can host one kind of session, and why, in plain words: "Chrome 131 at /usr/bin/google-chrome",
"Android SDK at ~/Android/Sdk, but no /dev/kvm".

data.description: At most 2 KB of JSON; the hub trims before emitting.

oneOf.description: The machine's node woke from sleep; `data.fromMs`, `data.toMs` (epoch milliseconds).

The machine's disk or load stopped new agents there, or no longer does; `data.paused`, and the summary says
why. Agents already running keep going.

Agents on the machine kept dying (claude exited, or stalled), so fleetd stopped resuming them there, or
resumes them again; `data` is `RecoveryPausedData`, and the summary says why.
The machine's node runs a session no task or lead of this hub owns; `data` is `ThreadOrphanedData`.
The node no longer has the project: the hub dropped it from its cache, and its open workstreams stop. `data.title`.
A project was added from a path or a finished clone: `data` is `ProjectAddedData` (the inspect line included).

A clone `project_add` accepted is running: `data` is `CloneProgressData`. Throttled; never stored past the
event log's own retention.
A clone `project_add` accepted failed: `data` is `ProjectAddFailedData`, with the fix.

A writer's worktree started from a stale base because git can't fetch the project's remote, or the remote names
no default branch. Once per project until a fetch works again; `data` is `tasks::FetchFailedData`.

A project's settings changed (`project_set`): `data.mediumAllowed`; or a repo was removed from it
(`project_repo_remove`): `data.repoRemoved`, its name.
Needs approval or user input.
A wake missed while the hub was down, with catchUp "skip".
A queued write to an offline machine was delivered when it came back.
A queued write outlived its TTL and was dropped.
The brief was set and the work started.
A lead needs a person for a secret or an approval; `data` is the request (RequestEventData).

A request changed state (stored, declined, approved, running, done, failed, denied, or open again when it could
not run); `data` as request.opened.
A person revoked a decision (`decisions_overturn`); its key goes unanswered again.
`data.queuedReason`.
A project's max agents or the fleet cap changed; `data` is `tasks::AgentsCapData`, `summary` the chat's line.
The lead closed it. `data.workstreamId`, `data.reason` (why) and `data.by`.
`data.taskId`, `data.prHeadSha`, `data.blocking`.
`data.changeId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`.
A clean review is bound to its current patch id. `data.changeId`.
The PR conflicts with its base, or with the PRs ahead of it in a batch; `data.changeId`.
`data.changeId`, `data.checks` (failing check names), `data.logUrl`.

`data.changeId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`, `data.mergedSha`; `data.ci` when the repo had no CI and the
train merged on fleetd's own checks.

A PR was merged into a base the train guards without the train; `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`,
`data.mergedSha`, and `data.changeId` when it had been enqueued. Newer hubs add `data.mergedAt`, `data.head`,
`data.base`, `data.prCreatedAt`, `data.authorKind`, `data.mergedByKind` and `data.mergedBy` (the merger's login).
Refused at enqueue; `data.prUrl`, `data.fix`.
M4: a machine's login hit the same limit on several threads, or its proxy has no account; dispatch there pauses.
M4: parked threads were sent "continue" at their reset or on usage_resume; `data.breakerCleared`.
M11: doctor checks changed status; `data.changes` lists `{ id, from, to }` (from absent on the first run).

A device redeemed a pairing code from `fleetd pair` or an invite and got a human key; `data.keyId`,
`data.deviceName`, `data.personId` (absent from a hub before people), `data.inviteId` (an invite's).

A prompt override was saved or reset: `data.id`, `data.scope`, `data.projectRef`, `data.ref` (absent on reset),
`data.warnings` (their codes). The text is not in the event; prompt_get reads it.

This release changed the default of a prompt you overrode; yours stays in effect until you save it again or
reset it: `data.id`, `data.scope`, `data.projectRef`, `data.base`, `data.current`.

A steer was stored (or put in the offline queue). `data` is a `SteerEventData`, plus `data.text` (first 120
characters), `data.mode` and `data.by`.
claude took the steer in; `data.how`.
The agent replied after taking it in (`data.excerpt`), or a lead call named it.
The steer's run ended with no reply after it was delivered.

Refused by the node, the process exited before taking it in, or it expired in the offline queue;
`data.reason`.
No longer sent (plans were removed); kept so an older log still reads.
No longer sent (plans were removed); kept so an older log still reads.

A merge-train Change moved between states; `data.changeId`, `data.workstreamId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`,
`data.from`, `data.to`.
Main-branch CI of a train repo changed state; `data.repo`, `data.sha`, `data.state`, `data.failing`.
A status source went quiet past its cadence; `data.source`, `data.sinceMs`, `data.reason`.
A stale source answered again; `data.source`, `data.staleMs`.

A project's chat got a message, or one of its messages finished streaming or had an inline item change state;
`data` is `chat::ChatMessageEventData`.

A project's chat started or stopped waiting on you, or its lead started or ended a turn; `data` is the
`chat::ProjectChatState`.

The app was focused on a project's screen with recent input, for one interval; `data` is
`metrics::AppPresenceData`. A human touch for the factory metrics.
A node's fetch saw a remote's default branch move; `data` is `metrics::RepoAdvancedData`.
Work was claimed on a repo's base; `data` is `work::WorkEventData`.
A claim landed, was released or expired; `data` is `work::WorkEventData`.

A commit reached a watched base, by the train, a PR merged outside it or a direct push; `data` is
`work::WorkLandedData`.

A memory file changed (a lead's `remember`, an Undo, an edit in the app): `data.scope`, `data.projectRef`
(project scope), `data.topic`, `data.by`. The text is not in the event; memory_get reads it.

An automation was made, edited, paused, resumed, deleted or had its webhook URL rotated: `data.projectRef`,
`data.automationId`, `data.change`. automation_list reads it.

An automation ran (its order opened) or a trigger was skipped: `data.projectRef`, `data.automationId`,
`data.runId`, `data.trigger`, `data.state`, `data.workstreamId`. Never the webhook body.
A project's checklist changed (the lead's `checklist`); `data` is `checklist::ChecklistChangedData`.

A hub-kept skill was created, edited, installed, updated or deleted: `data.scope`, `data.projectRef` (project
scope), `data.names`, `data.by`. skills_list reads them.

A browser session started, changed hands, ended, or its recording landed or was lost; `data` is
`browser::BrowserSessionEventData`. browser_sessions reads the rest.

A preview started, moved a step, became ready, ended or failed; `data` is `preview::PreviewEventData`.
previews_list reads the rest.

A person was invited, joined, renamed, given another role or removed, an invite was revoked, or a device signed
out; `data` is `people::PeopleChangedData`. people_list reads the rest.

fix.description: The command a person runs to fix it, when there is one.

message.description: Plain words: the runtime and device sessions use, or what is wrong.

IosState.description: Where a node's iOS sessions stand, for the doctor.

oneOf.description: The golden simulator is made: sessions start.
Xcode and an iOS runtime work, but the machine isn't opted in: node.json's `ios.enabled` makes the golden.
Making the golden simulator: one boot left to settle, and agent-device's runner built for it.
Can't run here until a person fixes something (no Xcode, no iOS runtime, no Node.js, or the golden failed).
A permission prompt waits on a person.
Usage limit: resumes at the reset.

LiveFrame.description:
Hub -> app on the live subscription. Board lanes at most 1/s, focus lanes and text at most 4/s; machines at most
every 5 s and slots at most 1/s, each only when changed. A slow link skips frames (latest wins), never queues them.

at.description: The hub's clock; the app derives its skew from it.

full.description: The first frame after a (re)subscribe: every lane in scope. Lanes not in a full frame are gone.

machines.description: Present when any machine changed (always in a full frame).

slots.description: Present when the slot board changed (always in a full frame, once the hub runs slots).

LiveLane.description: One lane's live values. In a frame that is not `full`, only lanes that changed are sent.

activity.description: Absent: nothing to say (no run active, or no recent model output; the UI says no more than the status).

spark.description: Absent: unchanged since the last frame (always present in a `full` frame for lanes that have one).

LiveText.description:
Streamed assistant text of the focused order's lanes and lead: append to `message_id`'s text. The complete
message replaces it when the thread tail is refetched.

LoginLimit.description: One claude.ai usage window, as claude's `rate_limit_event` last reported it.

limitType.description: claude's own name for the window, e.g. "five_hour", "seven_day".

observedAt.description: When claude reported it; absent from older nodes. Without it a reading's age is unknown.

utilization.description: 0 to 1 as claude sends it; absent when it sent none.

boxPubKey.description:
M8: the node's X25519 key from its hello; clients seal this machine's secrets to it. Absent: it takes no
secrets.

degradedReason.description: Plain language, set while status is "degraded".

lastSlept.description: The machine's latest sleep its node reported on waking.

MachineLive.description: A machine's load and running agents, from its heartbeat (every 15 s) and the hub's executors.

load.description: Absent: the node does not report load (older node, or the read failed). Show no load then.

slept.description: Its latest sleep; show it while recent ([`crate::model::SleptSpan::recent_text`]).

NodeDisk.description: Space on the volume holding a node's worktrees and build cache.

minFreeBytes.description:
Below this the hub starts no new agents there: node.json's `minFreeGb`, else 10% of the volume or 20 GB,
whichever is larger.

NodeLoad.description: What a machine reports about itself with each heartbeat.

android.description: Whether the machine can host android sessions; absent where node.json turns them off and from older nodes.

desktop.description:
Whether the machine can host Linux desktop sessions, and in what; absent where node.json turns them off and
from older nodes.

disk.description: The volume holding the node's worktrees and build cache; absent from older nodes and when it can't be read.

diskPerAgentBytes.description: Disk to allow per new agent's worktree: node.json's `diskPerAgentGb`, else 5 GB. Absent from older nodes.

hosts.description:
What the machine can host for sessions (a browser, an Android emulator, an iOS simulator, a desktop); absent
from older nodes.

ios.description:
Whether the machine can host iOS sessions; absent off macOS, where node.json turns them off, on a Mac without
Xcode that didn't opt in, and from older nodes.

limits.description:
The latest claude.ai subscription limit of each type claude reported. Empty behind API keys and gateways,
which send none.

memPerAgentBytes.description:
Memory to allow per agent when sizing the machine's cap: node.json's `memPerAgentGb`, else 2 GB. Absent from
older nodes.

memPressurePct.description:
Memory pressure: the share of the last 10 s in which some task stalled waiting for memory (PSI `some avg10`),
percent. Linux only; absent on kernels without PSI and from older nodes.

memTotalBytes.description: Physical memory; absent from older nodes and when it can't be read.

memUsedPct.description: Memory in use (total minus available), percent.

swapUsedPct.description: Swap in use, percent. Linux only; absent without swap and from older nodes.

NotifyPolicy.description:
When a client may interrupt the human with an event marked `attention`. Quiet windows are absolute times the
hub computes from `policy.quiet_hours` in `policy.tz`: the one under way (if any) and the next.

coalesceSec.description: At most one notification per this many seconds; what arrives meanwhile is folded into the next.

quiet.description:
Only "urgent" events notify inside these; empty when quiet hours are off. Ask again after the last one ends
or on decision.recorded.

ProjectChatState.description: One chat's state, for the sidebar and the status row.

lastSeq.description: The newest message's `seq`; 0 for an empty chat.

needsYou.description: The lead's last message waits for a human reply, or an inline item is open.

nudges.description: The nudges still waiting to be seen, oldest first: what the app shows as "N to look at". Absent when none is.

openItems.description:
The inline items still open, oldest first, however far back: the chat may not have their page loaded. Absent
when none is (and from older hubs).

ProjectRef.description:
A project: a workspace with a lead and its own directory, on its home machine, where the lead runs. Its
`projectId` is the node's id for that directory, so the ref also addresses the files; the directory may be a git
repo or a plain folder. A project holds zero or more repos (`ProjectRepo`), each in a node directory of its
own or in the project's.

base.description: The branch its work lands on; absent until fleetd knows it.

checkout.description:
The node's directory holding its files: the project's own `ProjectRef` when the project's directory is this
repo.

path.description: The checkout's directory on its machine; absent before its node reported it.

repoKey.description: Its origin remote, shortened; absent for a repo with no remote, or before fleetd has read it.

repos.description: The git repos it holds, from the hub; none for a plain directory, from a node, and from an older hub.

SessionHost.description: A kind of session a machine can host.

oneOf.description: A fresh Chrome per session.
An Android emulator: the Android SDK, with KVM on Linux.
An iOS simulator: Xcode on macOS.
A Linux desktop: docker or Xvfb.

SleptSpan.description: A span a machine spent asleep, epoch milliseconds; `machine.slept` carries the same fields as its data.

cap.description: Agents running at once across every project: `fleetCap` when set, else the sum of the machines' caps.

fleetCap.description: The fleet cap a person (or an older hub) saved; absent: none beyond the machines' own caps.

SlotStatePerMachine.description: One machine's share of the board: what it fits, and what runs there.

auto.description:
What the machine fits: one agent per CPU less a reserve, and 2 GB of memory each after the OS's share, at
most 64.

cap.description: The most agents that run on it at once: a person's setting for the machine, else `auto`.

diskRoom.description: New agents its free disk has room for now, above the guard's floor; absent while the node reports no disk.

maxAgents.description: A person's setting for the machine (`cap_set`); absent: it runs `auto`.

why.description: The term that sets `auto`, e.g. "memory 18 GB, about 2 GB an agent" or "14 of 16 CPUs".

maxAgents.description:
The most of the project's agents (its tasks: writers, readers, reviewers) that run at once; its lead is not
one. Until set, the default: its machine's `cap`, within the fleet cap.

own.description:
A person set the project's own max; false: it follows the default. Absent from a hub before this, which
listed a project only once set or busy.

queued.description: Its agents waiting for a slot, paused ones included.

running.description: Its agents running now. Above `maxAgents` right after the cap was lowered: nothing is stopped for it.

Spark.description:
Work per 2 s bucket, oldest first, ending with the bucket that ends at `end_at`. A sample is
`min(255, 16 × items started + streamed chars / 32 + output tokens not streamed as text / 8)`; a bucket with
no frames is 0.

Tokens.description: Summed over the lane's runs. `live`: the running run's usage is streaming in (else it updates at each run's end).
